identity.name: Session Manager
identity.oneLine: Electron desktop cockpit for driving Claude Code CLI sessions across projects via a TAB→Epic→PRD hierarchy, with scheduling, chat/terminal views, and mobile relay.
identity.claim: A local cockpit for Claude Code.
identity.sub: Terminal + 25+ config/observability/scheduling tabs (Settings, Skills, Hooks, MCP Servers, Tasks, Plans, History, Scheduler, Memory, Permissions, etc.), plus a mobile web cockpit at bilko.run. Runs on your machine — the fs layer never writes outside the home directory, and Project Pages ship with zero network egress.
identity.audience: For developers running Claude Code CLI sessions across multiple projects

pillars.d: A Terminal tab is anchored to one cwd; that cwd IS the project identity, and every skill, hook and permission scopes itself to it automatically.
status: 'proposed' is the human approval gate — an agent files a proposed Epic instead of writing into a feedback inbox; nothing runs until a human presses Approve & start.

pillars.t: A scheduler that respects the billing window
pillars.d: Approved PRDs run as claude -p jobs from a ≤3-deep machine-wide session slot pool, auto-pausing on rate-limit and resuming at the next 5h reset.

pillars.t: Single-writer law over the ops root
pillars.d: Every session-manager-operations/<namespace> folder has exactly one owning surface that may write it — fail-closed, enforced in opsOwnership.cjs.

feature.name: Scheduler Redesign (Almanac / Canvas-2)
feature.oneLine: The Scheduler tab's Canvas-2 restyle, paired with structural fixes that make an Epic's proposed→active transition and its on-disk index un-corruptible.
feature.problem: Scheduler/Plans/Background-Agents had grown into three overlapping nav destinations, and nothing stopped an Epic from being minted directly into 'active' or a concurrent write from clobbering active-index.json.
feature.solution: Scheduler/Plans/Background-Agents were merged into one Scheduler destination (2026-06-03), then restyled around the Almanac/Canvas-2 design system. ensureEpic and createPromptSession were made structurally unable to mint an Epic as anything but 'proposed', and persistActiveIndex became a read-merge-write instead of a blind overwrite.

steps.d: Scheduler/Plans/Background-Agents merged into one Scheduler destination; Home-tab vs Project-tab left-nav split out.
f559d59 — Scheduler rebuilt around the Canvas-2 design: Machine destination, first-run guide, merged diagnostics.
b2b1b82 / 92280db / 3d12e19 — ensureEpic and persistActiveIndex made structurally unable to mint or overwrite an Epic into 'active'.
Actions dropdown menu, Build toolbar button and a discuss-first path replaced the prior scattered row controls.
1c8f5ed — New Epic card now separates agentType (who runs the session) from tag/mission (what it's for), with a flip-layout grounding board inspector.

rules.d: proposed / active / completed — no draft state; a half-typed Epic is proposed.
Enforced structurally in ensureEpic and createPromptSession, not just by convention.
active-index.json writes never blind-overwrite; a race can no longer drop another writer's session.
A zustand selector must never build a fresh array/object per call — three prior blank-app incidents, guarded by npm run lint:selectors.

faq.q: Can an Epic be created directly as active?
faq.a: No — ensureEpic and createPromptSession are structurally unable to do that; every Epic is born proposed (b2b1b82, 92280db).

faq.q: What happens if active-index.json is written by two processes at once?
faq.a: persistActiveIndex has been a read-merge-write since 3d12e19, so a race no longer drops the other writer's session.

faq.q: Where did the feedback folder go?
faq.a: It's retired — status: 'proposed' Epics are the human-approval gate now; nothing runs until Approve & start is pressed.

architecture.summary: An Electron main process owns the claude CLI session pool, the scheduler queue and the fs layer; a React renderer talks to it only over typed, zod-validated IPC channels — neither side touches the other's concern directly.

principles.d: Every session-manager-operations/<namespace> has exactly one owning surface; a write by an undeclared writer throws (opsOwnership.cjs, fail-closed).
All fs writes go through config.cjs's writeJson/writeTextAtomic (tmp + rename) — no ad hoc fs.writeFile in app-owned state.
Renderer zustand stores never cross-subscribe; components compose multiple stores via hooks/selectors instead.
A tab IS a cwd; every nav destination, skill and permission derives from the focused project, not global config.

layers.d: React tabs/state/components — Terminal, Scheduler, Epics, Project Home, Config
ipcSchemas.cjs — zod-validated channels between renderer and main
Session pool, scheduler, queue store, hooks runner, transcripts, config fs layer
claude binary, project cwds, session-manager-operations/, ~/.claude config tree

modules.d: Epic lifecycle state — status transitions, rename/delete guards
runs PRDs as claude -p jobs; boot reconciliation, dead-process reaper, feedback sweep
Main-process IPC surface for Epic lifecycle

flow.n: events published after every state change
selectors read raw slices only, then derive in the component

decisions.w: architecture/, design-mocks/, HUMAN_LEARN/, reviews/ stay outside the single-writer law as skill-authored documentation, not app-owned runtime state (decided 2026-07-31).

decisions.t: project-pages/ is not an OWNERS namespace either
decisions.w: Written directly by a project-home-builder Epic's own Write tool calls, never through config.cjs — no app-enforceable concurrent-write hazard to guard.
No draft state; a half-typed Epic is proposed. Enforced structurally in ensureEpic/createPromptSession rather than left to convention.
